The period from 2011 to 2013 appears to have been marked by an increase in political sensitivity in Azerbaijan.
The increase in political sensitivity in Azerbaijan from 2011 to 2013 was generated, inter alia, by the presidential elections, which took place in October 2013.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, titled 'The honouring of obligations and commitments by Azerbaijan', expressed concern that recently adopted amendments to the Criminal Code and the Administrative Code had increased penalties for the organisers of, and participants in, unauthorised gatherings.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that, considering the authorities' ongoing blanket ban on protests in the Baku city centre, the amendments increasing penalties for organisers of and participants in unauthorised gatherings were likely to have a further negative impact on freedom of assembly and freedom of expression.
Resolution 2062 (2015) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, titled 'The functioning of democratic institutions in Azerbaijan', was adopted on 23 June 2015.

On various dates the applicants lodged appeals with the Baku Court of Appeal, presenting their version of the facts surrounding their arrests.

The first, second, third, fifth and sixth applicants argued before the Baku Court of Appeal that they had been unlawfully arrested for their political activity, including their active participation in demonstrations.
The fourth applicant argued before the Baku Court of Appeal that he had been unlawfully arrested for the comments he had posted on social media.
The applicants complained before the Baku Court of Appeal that the hearings before the respective first-instance courts had not been fair.
The fifth applicant submitted to the Baku Court of Appeal that previously he had given self-incriminatory statements for fear of being framed for the offence of illegal possession of drugs.
The fifth applicant complained to the Baku Court of Appeal that he had been kept in the police station overnight from 5 to 6 March 2014 without any official decision or record of his detention.
All the applicants were represented before the Baku Court of Appeal by lawyers of their own choosing.
